Header banner for /pages/pdrn-research. Replaces skingenetix-philosophy-research.jpg — an image lifted off the philosophy page, showing an open journal and amber vials, which is neither this molecule nor this palette.

ON-SYSTEM WITH THE SIBLING RESEARCH PAGES. Copper Peptide research runs graphite plus its own clinical blue; Matrixyl research runs graphite plus its own teal. The art direction says a research page takes its molecule's scene colour, so this one is graphite #1A1A1A plus PDRN's blush pink #F3BFC2.

BAND MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The live band on this page is 1440x454 and 1920x454 — 3.17:1 and 4.23:1. The Matrixyl research band is 496px tall, so its numbers do not transfer. Generating at 3072x700 (4.389:1) clears the 4.23:1 the widest viewport needs, with a little margin for object-position to aim.

RESERVED TYPE ZONE, measured as a fraction. The left 40% of every frame is held as near-empty graphite so a headline sits on it unaided. This is rule 2 of the five production constraints, and unlike the ingredient tiles — where type renders below the image — it genuinely applies here, because the heading is overlaid.

THE WORD SALMON APPEARS NOWHERE IN THESE BRIEFS, deliberately. PDRN is salmon-derived and the page copy says so, but naming the source in an image brief invites a fish, and this is a clinical research page. The material is described instead: fine translucent strands, a double helix, a repairing membrane.

PDRN NAMES THE DOUBLE HELIX, as its ingredient tile does. The standing rule here is describe-don't-name, but PDRN is sodium DNA, so the stock idea IS the subject; the brief names it AND describes the geometry, which pins the form without inviting clip-art. This is unrelated to the brand's helix mark, which stays dots-and-dashes and never appears in a Class B frame.

slots.title: One double helix, right of frame, graphite left
slots.prompt: Wide cinematic scientific photograph on a seamless graphite ground (#1A1A1A) that runs out to all four edges. One DNA double helix stands in the RIGHT THIRD of the frame, running from the top edge down toward the lower right: two smooth strands winding around a common axis in a regular repeating twist, joined at even intervals by short straight rungs between them. It is rendered in soft blush pink (#F3BFC2), rim-lit so its near edges glow against the dark and its far turns fall away into shadow. The LEFT 40% OF THE FRAME IS EMPTY GRAPHITE at an even tone, holding no structure at all. A single hard key light from the upper right rakes across the helix and lays a soft shadow to the left; nothing else is lit. Clinical, rigorous and expensive — a research laboratory, not a spa.
slots.negative_extra: helix at the centre, helix on the left, structure filling the left side, symmetrical composition

slots.title: Fine strands drifting, dense right, dissolving left
slots.prompt: Wide cinematic scientific photograph on a seamless graphite ground (#1A1A1A). Extremely fine translucent strands drift and curl through the RIGHT HALF of the frame at different depths, some crossing and looping past one another, each catching a soft blush pink (#F3BFC2) rim light along its length. They thin out and dissolve completely as they travel left, so the LEFT 40% OF THE FRAME IS EMPTY GRAPHITE at an even tone. The nearest strands are razor sharp and the deeper ones fall away into shadow. A single hard key light from the upper right; nothing else is lit. Clinical, rigorous and expensive — a research laboratory, not a spa.

slots.title: A fine membrane knitting closed — renewal
slots.prompt: Wide cinematic scientific photograph on a seamless graphite ground (#1A1A1A). In the RIGHT HALF of the frame, an extremely fine translucent membrane is drawing closed across a gap: fine filaments reach from both sides and interlace where they meet, denser and more complete toward the right edge and progressively more open toward the middle. The filaments carry a soft blush pink (#F3BFC2) glow along their lit edges. The LEFT 40% OF THE FRAME IS EMPTY GRAPHITE at an even tone, with no structure. A single hard key light from the upper right rakes across the membrane; the deeper layers fall into shadow. Clinical, rigorous and expensive — a research laboratory, not a spa.
